hints: Notice the graph is momentum in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ against time in $\text{s}$, rising straight from 0 to 5000 in 10 s.
Recall that resultant force equals rate of change of momentum, so $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$ is the gradient of this graph.
Calculate the gradient as $(5000 - 0)/(10 - 0)$ and check the unit gives $\text{N}$.
walkthrough: Read the straight-line graph: change in momentum $\Delta p = 5000 - 0 = 5000$ $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ in time $\Delta t = 10 - 0 = 10$ $\text{s}$.
State the governing rule: resultant force equals rate of change of momentum, $F = \Delta p / \Delta t$.
Substitute the values with units: $F = 5000/10$ $\text{kg m s}^{-1}/\text{s}$.

options.A: Gradient is $5000/10 = 500$ $\text{N}$, which equals the rate of change of momentum.
options.B: 5000 is the final momentum in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$, not the rate of change of momentum.
options.C: 25000 is half the product of momentum and time, which is the area under the graph and not force.
options.D: 50000 is the product $5000 \times 10$, which multiplies change in momentum by time instead of dividing.
